name: The Undercroft
formed_by_story: The Oroth foundation Tollmere is built on. The guilds cut sewers into it because it was easier than cutting new stone, and stopped where the old work refused the pick.
who_was_here: Everyone, eventually. Clerks dumping ledgers, thieves keeping them, and the Builders who laid the floor nobody has managed to lift.
story: Under the city, a hall inside a bell. The Quiet Hands took the Undercroft because it is the one place in Tollmere the Tallymen cannot price: no charter covers ground that predates the charter. The hinge-less door at the far end opens for names, and the Hands have been guessing at names for eighty years.
unique_object: the Unsaid Ledger: every price the law of Tollmere has ever taken, in eleven hands

beats.note: A canal grate, dropped through from Lantern Row. The ladder is a rope, and it is not always there.
Guild sewer: brick above, Oroth stone below, and the join is a straight line nobody cut.
A flooded cistern with a walkway two handspans wide around it. Gutter drakes nest in the brick.
Where the guilds threw their old ledgers. Waist-deep in paper. Every sheet is a price.
The Hands' hall, inside a bell the size of a guildhall, hung mouth-down in the foundation. They light it with stolen lamps and nobody speaks above the note it still holds.
Oroth steps, each one exactly a handspan, descending past three sealed doors.
The hinge-less door. Nine name-slots in its face, six of them filled with names that did not work.
A collapsed side-vault the drakes have made their own, floored in fishbones and coins.
A shaft the Hands cut to Gull Lane, barred at the top by a grate only they have the key to.

shortcut.note: Opens from inside. The Hands will pretend they always meant you to have it.

encounters.note: Gutter drakes, in the bestiary's terms a pack; they come along the walkway so only two can reach you.
The Guild's two bravos, paid to stand in a room nobody can get into; they have been playing at counters for nine years and are very fast.
